newsitem.title: UK: Merrydown profits hit by fall in 'alcopops'.
newsitem.headline: Merrydown profits hit by fall in 'alcopops'.

text.p: British drinks manufacturer Merrydown Plc said on Friday that annual profits were undermined by a decline in the sale of its 'Two Dogs' brand, one of the so called "alcopops", which has caused controversy in recent months over under-age drinking.

Overall pre-tax profits at the group slipped to 820,000 pounds from 2.03 million previously. Annual sales slipped six percent to 34.9 million and the company cut its total dividend payment to 3.10 pence per share from 4.50 pence.
"The market for alcoholic carbonates rapidly became overcrowded, as well as intensely competitive, and it has became increasingly difficult to maintain distribution," said the company in a statement.
Merrydown warned back in May that its results for the year to March 31, 1997 would come in below market expectations and said that 'Two Dogs' had not lived up to expectations in the last quarter.

It said that a seasonal downturn in demand in the final quarter fell well short of the level that importers had originally anticipated. Alcopop sales are worth around 265 million pounds a year to the drinks industry.
An 80 percent increase in excise duty in the UK's November budget also hit 'Two Dogs'.
Sales of the drink have continued to fall in the first quarter on uncertainty surrounding the future of the whole alcoholic carbonates market, said the firm.

UK Home Secretary Jack Straw called for an urgent inquiry into the consumption of alcopops on May 16 and the Co-operative Wholesale Society has banned the sale of alcopops from its 1,200 licenced stores.
But the firm welcomed the government's plans, announced at the July budget, to carry out a full review of excise duties across all alcoholic drink sectors.
Merrydown, which also makes Merrydown ciders and Shloer brands, said that current sales of cider have continued at "satisfactory levels" and that the outlook for Shloer remains solid.
